title: Mallard Duck Movement
text:
Mallard ducks (Anas platyrhynchos) are adaptable dabbling ducks found across much of the Northern Hemisphere. They use wetlands, lakes, and rivers for feeding, resting, and breeding, and their movements can change with season and habitat.
Lake Constance is a large freshwater lake in Central Europe, bordered by Germany, Switzerland, and Austria. Its varied shoreline and location along important waterbird routes make it a useful setting for studying duck movement.
The GPS tracking data records where individual mallards travel over time, along with their speed and direction. These observations reveal the geographic range of the tracked birds, differences among individuals, and seasonal patterns in their movement.
